items.title: Where the local process waits is unknown
items.whyItMatters: Another unit found the longest wait at physician approval (claim c1), but this unit has never mapped its morning.
items.opportunity: Map the value stream with gemba walks at 07:00 on five mornings before choosing countermeasures.

items.title: Reminders improve paperwork, not practice
items.whyItMatters: The screen is already documented on 71 percent of days, and a reminder elsewhere changed documentation only (claim c2).
items.opportunity: Measure completed interruptions, not documented screens, as the primary measure.

items.title: Fear of self-extubation
items.whyItMatters: Nurses fear harm although self-extubation is rare (claim c3); without a visible safety measure the fear will persist.
items.opportunity: Track self-extubation and agitation needing a bolus as balancing measures and share them at huddles.

items.title: Families at the bedside
items.whyItMatters: Interruptions are skipped when families are present, and families who speak another language may not be told what awakening involves.
items.opportunity: Add a short explanation for families, with interpreter access, to the morning routine.

items.title: Paired breathing trials lag behind
items.whyItMatters: Only 29 percent of eligible days have a paired breathing trial.
items.opportunity: Test a shared morning time with respiratory therapy (claim c4).

errorsFound: The documented reason 'physician preference' hides an approval step that the protocol does not require.
reevaluation: The gaps favour mapping the morning before changing it, with countermeasures aimed at the waits after the screen and safety measures kept visible.
summary: Five gaps; the unknown location of the local wait is high severity.
